name: Blaise Hamlet

dates.note: THE DATE IS ON RECORD THREE WAYS AND NONE IS RESOLVED. Both list entries read here open 'Cottage. 1812. By John Nash and George Repton. For JS Harford.' The node's exemplar gives 1811, the Wikipedia article says the hamlet 'was built around 1811', the National Trust page says 'built in 1811', and a heritage guide read the same day says Nash designed it 'in 1809'. The list entries are the only sources here that state a year without hedging, and they say 1812.

refs.title: Blaise Hamlet, Circular Cottage, Non Civil Parish - 1202262 | Historic England
refs.note: The record's survey block. A search result the same day printed its Official list entry field values as 'Grade: I ; List Entry Number: 1202262 ; Date first listed: 08-Jan-1959 ; List Entry Name: Blaise Hamlet, Circular Cottage'. The entry's Sources block cites 'Temple, N, John Nash and the Village Picturesque, (1979)' and 'Pevsner, N, The Buildings of England: North Somerset and Bristol, (1958), 468'.

refs.title: Blaise Hamlet, Diamond Cottage, Non Civil Parish - Historic England
refs.note: A second cottage, read as continuous prose in an extract, AND IT CONTRADICTS THE NODE. Its statutory address is 'BLAISE HAMLET, DIAMOND COTTAGE, 2, HALLEN ROAD' and its description reads 'Cottage. 1812. By John Nash and George Repton. For JS Harford. Random rubble with brick lateral stacks and a stone-tiled hipped roof. Single-depth plan. Picturesque style. Single-storey and attic; 1-window range.' The node's exemplar says the nine cottages each have 'a different thatch'; this one is roofed in stone tiles and not thatched at all. The Wikipedia article agrees with the entry rather than the node: 'The cottages are each unique and have brick chimneys and dormer windows, with some having thatched roofs.'

refs.title: Blaise Hamlet - Wikipedia
refs.note: Read as a search result. It states that the hamlet is 'a group of nine small cottages around a green in Henbury' and that 'All the cottages, and the sundial on the green, are Grade I listed buildings.' A further Historic England reference exists for the sundial, 1202264, 'Sundial to the Middle of the Green at Blaise Hamlet', which was seen in a search result and not extracted.

quotes.text: Paired lattice casements, to the sides and front, and half-dormers to the left and front. Paired diagonally-set rear stacks. C20 tiled rear extension.
quotes.page: Official list entry, Details, description continued

quotes.text: INTERIOR not inspected, but reported as having a winder stair flight, sitting room and pantry.

Arranged by Harford for his retired employees. Part of an irregular composition forming '...the nec plus ultra of picturesque layout and design,' (Pevsner). The cottages are laid out around an open green, and were modernised c1975.

measurements.note: The deep sheltering eave the node's own constraint calls a 'good hat'. It is the one place in this cluster where an entry states how far round a building an overhang runs, and it still gives no dimension.

measurements.name: interior_room_count
measurements.as_printed: a winder stair flight, sitting room and pantry
measurements.note: NO COUNT IS PARSED. The entry names a winder stair, a sitting room and a pantry and says plainly that the interior was NOT inspected and that this is reported rather than seen, so counting rooms from it would be an inference wearing a survey's authority. It is carried because the winder stair behind the fire is the node's own lobby-entry description, arriving in a picturesque cottage of 1812.

The survey block is Circular Cottage because a group record may carry one survey item and quoting several under one number would be uncheckable; Diamond Cottage is quoted in its own reference note, where it contradicts the node's claim that every cottage is thatched.
